fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. John 12:2 says Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with Jesus. This is the man Jesus had raised from the dead, and now he's reclining at a dinner table. I think that's the best seat in the house.

Not shoulders, baker. John 12:3 says Mary anointed Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair. It's a small detail, but it's right there in the verse. I'd have guessed wrong too, because I keep picturing a hat on my head and a cookie on my shoulder.

Good guess, friend, but that's a different word. Peter denied Jesus later (Luke 22:61), and the Gospel of Mark lists Peter among the twelve He appointed (Mark 3:14, 16). John 12:4 says Judas Iscariot was going to betray Him. Easy to mix up two men in one group chat.
Not a spy, friend. John 12:6 says Judas did not say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. The verse puts it plainly, and it says thief. No trench coat needed.
Nope, baker, no mail route for Judas. John 12:6 says he was the keeper of the money bag. He had asked why the perfume wasn't sold for three hundred denarii (John 12:5).

Yes, baker. The crowd came not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead (John 12:9). People were coming to see a man Jesus had raised from the dead. I'd be hiding in the pantry.

Good thought, friend, but Martha isn't who they came to see. John 12:9 says they came to see Lazarus, whom Jesus had raised from the dead. Martha is the one John 12:2 says served at the dinner. The crowd came because of Jesus and because of Lazarus.
